lessons.title: Regions
lessons.summary: What is an AWS Region? A geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Regional service availability and requirements should be verified.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A recovery plan assumes resources exist in a second Region. Inventory regional dependencies and explicitly provision the recovery environment.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every Region shares one physical data center. This is not a sound assumption; a geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones.

lessons.takeaway: Regional service availability and requirements should be verified.

lessons.title: Availability Zones
lessons.summary: Why distribute workloads across Availability Zones? Reduce exposure to a single zone failure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Applications still need sufficient surviving capacity.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A zone outage removes half the service capacity. Verify surviving capacity and cross-zone application behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Two instances in one zone guarantee zone-failure tolerance. This is not a sound assumption; reduce exposure to a single zone failure.

lessons.takeaway: Applications still need sufficient surviving capacity.

lessons.title: IAM roles
lessons.summary: Why prefer roles with temporary credentials for workloads? Reduce dependence on embedded long-lived access keys.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Role permissions should match the workload's required actions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An application image contains a long-lived AWS access key. Use an appropriate workload role and rotate the exposed key.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Roles always grant administrator access. This is not a sound assumption; reduce dependence on embedded long-lived access keys.

lessons.takeaway: Role permissions should match the workload's required actions.

lessons.title: Least privilege
lessons.summary: What is the goal of least-privilege IAM policies? Allow only required actions on intended resources under appropriate conditions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Explicit denies can override otherwise allowed actions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service can delete unrelated production resources. Narrow actions resources and conditions after verifying actual needs.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An allow statement always overrides every explicit deny. This is not a sound assumption; allow only required actions on intended resources under appropriate conditions.

lessons.takeaway: Explicit denies can override otherwise allowed actions.

lessons.title: S3 storage
lessons.summary: What storage model does Amazon S3 primarily provide? Object storage addressed through buckets and object keys.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Object storage differs from a local POSIX filesystem.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An application assumes S3 supports local filesystem locking semantics. Review the object API and redesign the storage interaction appropriately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An S3 bucket is automatically a mounted block device. This is not a sound assumption; object storage addressed through buckets and object keys.

lessons.takeaway: Object storage differs from a local POSIX filesystem.

lessons.title: EBS
lessons.summary: What is a common use of Amazon EBS? Block storage for EC2 workloads.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Volume durability does not replace independent backups.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An EC2 database needs recoverable persistent block storage. Choose suitable volumes and implement tested snapshot or backup recovery.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An EBS volume is automatically a global shared filesystem. This is not a sound assumption; block storage for EC2 workloads.

lessons.takeaway: Volume durability does not replace independent backups.

lessons.title: Security groups
lessons.summary: How do security groups generally filter traffic? Stateful rules allow specified traffic for associated resources.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rules should be scoped to required sources and ports.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A database security group allows inbound traffic from everywhere. Restrict sources to intended application identities or network ranges.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Security groups are stateless subnet-wide deny lists. This is not a sound assumption; stateful rules allow specified traffic for associated resources.

lessons.takeaway: Rules should be scoped to required sources and ports.

lessons.title: VPC subnets
lessons.summary: What makes a subnet public in the usual IPv4 routing sense? A route to an Internet Gateway supports direct Internet routing.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Instances also need appropriate addressing and security controls for reachability.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An instance in a public subnet cannot reach the Internet. Inspect addressing route table gateway and security controls.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A subnet name containing public automatically provides Internet access. This is not a sound assumption; a route to an Internet Gateway supports direct Internet routing.

lessons.takeaway: Instances also need appropriate addressing and security controls for reachability.

lessons.title: NAT gateways
lessons.summary: What is a typical purpose of a NAT gateway? Allow private-subnet workloads to initiate suitable outbound connections.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Outbound NAT does not by itself publish inbound application access.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A private workload needs outbound IPv4 access without a public address. Configure an appropriate NAT path and verify routes and security.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A NAT gateway is an inbound application load balancer. This is not a sound assumption; allow private-subnet workloads to initiate suitable outbound connections.

lessons.takeaway: Outbound NAT does not by itself publish inbound application access.

lessons.title: VPC endpoints
lessons.summary: Why use a VPC endpoint for a supported service? Provide a private connectivity path without relying on ordinary Internet egress.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Endpoint type policies DNS and service support affect behavior.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A private workload must access S3 without the planned NAT path. Evaluate the suitable endpoint and verify routing and authorization.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every endpoint supports every AWS service identically. This is not a sound assumption; provide a private connectivity path without relying on ordinary Internet egress.

lessons.takeaway: Endpoint type policies DNS and service support affect behavior.

lessons.title: Application Load Balancers
lessons.summary: What kind of routing is an ALB designed to support? Application-layer routing for protocols such as HTTP.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Healthy target selection depends on configured checks.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An ALB reports no healthy targets after deployment. Inspect target registration health-check settings and application responses.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: An ALB automatically makes every database query healthy. This is not a sound assumption; application-layer routing for protocols such as HTTP.

lessons.takeaway: Healthy target selection depends on configured checks.

lessons.title: Auto Scaling
lessons.summary: What should drive a useful scaling policy? A metric and target aligned with workload capacity needs.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Scaling requires warm-up time and downstream capacity.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Queue age grows while worker CPU remains low due to slow external calls. Choose a workload-relevant signal and investigate the dependency bottleneck.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Adding instances instantly fixes every bottleneck. This is not a sound assumption; a metric and target aligned with workload capacity needs.

lessons.takeaway: Scaling requires warm-up time and downstream capacity.

lessons.title: CloudWatch metrics
lessons.summary: What does a CloudWatch metric represent? Time-series measurements identified by namespace and dimensions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Resolution aggregation and dimensions influence interpretation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A dashboard combines different dimensions and hides one unhealthy instance. Inspect dimensions and aggregation alongside per-resource evidence.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every metric point is a complete application trace. This is not a sound assumption; time-series measurements identified by namespace and dimensions.

lessons.takeaway: Resolution aggregation and dimensions influence interpretation.

lessons.title: CloudTrail
lessons.summary: What is CloudTrail commonly used to investigate? AWS API activity and associated identity context.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Coverage and event configuration must match the required audit use case.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A resource was deleted and the responsible API caller is unknown. Inspect relevant audit events and confirm event coverage.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: CloudTrail is a replacement for all application logs. This is not a sound assumption; aWS API activity and associated identity context.

lessons.takeaway: Coverage and event configuration must match the required audit use case.

lessons.title: Shared responsibility
lessons.summary: What does AWS shared responsibility imply? AWS and customers own different security responsibilities.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Customer configuration data and identity controls remain important.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A public bucket exposes sensitive customer data. Correct customer-controlled access and investigate the exposure.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: AWS automatically secures every customer IAM policy. This is not a sound assumption; aWS and customers own different security responsibilities.

lessons.takeaway: Customer configuration data and identity controls remain important.

lessons.title: S3 versioning
lessons.summary: What can S3 versioning help recover from? Accidental overwrites or deletions when prior versions remain available.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Versioning still needs lifecycle cost and access considerations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An object was overwritten with incorrect content. Inspect retained versions and restore the intended one safely.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Versioning guarantees protection from every authorized destructive action. This is not a sound assumption; accidental overwrites or deletions when prior versions remain available.

lessons.takeaway: Versioning still needs lifecycle cost and access considerations.

lessons.title: RDS availability
lessons.summary: What is the main purpose of a standard RDS Multi-AZ deployment? Improve availability through managed standby and failover mechanisms.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Availability features do not replace application reconnect behavior and backups.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A database failover occurs and clients retain broken connections. Verify reconnect handling timeouts and recovery behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every standby is automatically a readable scaling replica. This is not a sound assumption; improve availability through managed standby and failover mechanisms.

lessons.takeaway: Availability features do not replace application reconnect behavior and backups.

lessons.title: Read replicas
lessons.summary: What is a common role of database read replicas? Offload eligible reads or support specific replication use cases.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Replication lag can affect freshness of reads.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Users read stale data immediately after a write. Review consistency requirements and route freshness-sensitive reads appropriately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: All replicas always provide immediately current writes. This is not a sound assumption; offload eligible reads or support specific replication use cases.

lessons.takeaway: Replication lag can affect freshness of reads.

lessons.title: Lambda retries
lessons.summary: Why design Lambda event processing for duplicate delivery where applicable? Event sources and retries can deliver work more than once.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Handlers should use idempotent operations for duplicate-sensitive effects.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An event triggers the same order action twice. Use an operation identity and durable deduplication strategy.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every Lambda event source guarantees exactly one execution. This is not a sound assumption; event sources and retries can deliver work more than once.

lessons.takeaway: Handlers should use idempotent operations for duplicate-sensitive effects.

lessons.title: SQS visibility
lessons.summary: What does SQS visibility timeout control? How long a received message is hidden from other consumers before deletion or expiry.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Processing longer than visibility can lead to duplicate concurrent work.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A long-running worker sees the same message processed elsewhere. Adjust or extend visibility appropriately and keep processing idempotent.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Receiving a message permanently deletes it. This is not a sound assumption; how long a received message is hidden from other consumers before deletion or expiry.

lessons.takeaway: Processing longer than visibility can lead to duplicate concurrent work.

lessons.title: Dead-letter queues
lessons.summary: What is a dead-letter queue useful for? Isolate repeatedly failing messages for investigation and recovery.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Redrive needs care to avoid replaying the same failure at scale.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Poison messages repeatedly fail and block useful processing. Inspect failures route them appropriately and define a controlled redrive.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A dead-letter queue automatically fixes malformed messages. This is not a sound assumption; isolate repeatedly failing messages for investigation and recovery.

lessons.takeaway: Redrive needs care to avoid replaying the same failure at scale.

lessons.title: DynamoDB keys
lessons.summary: Why is partition-key design important? It affects data distribution and access patterns.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A highly concentrated key can create a hot workload.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Most requests target one popular key and experience throttling. Inspect access concentration and redesign or shard the hot pattern where justified.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every partition key provides identical performance for every access pattern. This is not a sound assumption; it affects data distribution and access patterns.

lessons.takeaway: A highly concentrated key can create a hot workload.

lessons.title: KMS controls
lessons.summary: What is an important aspect of KMS authorization? Key policies and applicable identity permissions govern key use.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Encryption does not eliminate the need to control decrypt permissions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A workload can read object metadata but cannot decrypt the encrypted object. Inspect the key policy identity permissions and encryption context.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any user can decrypt data merely because it is encrypted. This is not a sound assumption; key policies and applicable identity permissions govern key use.

lessons.takeaway: Encryption does not eliminate the need to control decrypt permissions.

lessons.title: Secrets rotation
lessons.summary: What must accompany credential rotation? Consumers must obtain and use the updated credential correctly.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rotation should include validation and recovery behavior.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A rotated database credential breaks clients using a cached old value. Refresh consumer credentials and verify the rotation integration.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Changing a secret automatically updates every application cache. This is not a sound assumption; consumers must obtain and use the updated credential correctly.

lessons.takeaway: Rotation should include validation and recovery behavior.

lessons.title: Route 53 failover
lessons.summary: What is a limitation of DNS-based failover? Resolver caching and client behavior affect switchover timing.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Health checks must reflect the intended service failure conditions.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A failover record changes but some clients still reach the old endpoint. Inspect TTLs caches and client reconnect behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: DNS failover moves every established TCP connection instantly. This is not a sound assumption; resolver caching and client behavior affect switchover timing.

lessons.takeaway: Health checks must reflect the intended service failure conditions.

lessons.title: CloudFront caching
lessons.summary: Why include relevant request variation in cache policy? Different responses must not incorrectly share one cache entry.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Cache keys and origin behavior need deliberate alignment.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: One user's personalized response appears for another user. Disable unsafe caching and correct cache-key and response policy.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A cache always knows which cookies are security-sensitive. This is not a sound assumption; different responses must not incorrectly share one cache entry.

lessons.takeaway: Cache keys and origin behavior need deliberate alignment.

lessons.title: Cross-account access
lessons.summary: What must be evaluated for role assumption across accounts? The role trust relationship and caller authorization.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Trusting an account is distinct from granting every possible action.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A pipeline cannot assume a deployment role in another account. Inspect trust policy caller permissions and required conditions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A role name alone authorizes any external caller. This is not a sound assumption; the role trust relationship and caller authorization.

lessons.takeaway: Trusting an account is distinct from granting every possible action.

lessons.title: Service quotas
lessons.summary: Why include service quotas in capacity planning? Quota limits can block scaling even when the design is otherwise valid.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Quota increases and regional differences may require advance preparation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A surge triggers scaling but new capacity is rejected at a quota. Inspect the relevant quota and plan capacity or approved increases.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Auto Scaling bypasses every service quota. This is not a sound assumption; quota limits can block scaling even when the design is otherwise valid.

lessons.takeaway: Quota increases and regional differences may require advance preparation.

lessons.title: Cost attribution
lessons.summary: Why use cost allocation and workload ownership metadata? Connect spend to accountable services and teams.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Cost optimization should preserve required reliability and security.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An unexplained bill increase follows a new deployment. Attribute usage to resources and compare with workload changes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The lowest bill always represents the best architecture. This is not a sound assumption; connect spend to accountable services and teams.

lessons.takeaway: Cost optimization should preserve required reliability and security.

lessons.title: Disaster recovery
lessons.summary: What makes a second-Region recovery design credible? Tested recovery of data identities dependencies and traffic handling.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Recovery objectives must be measured in realistic exercises.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A regional exercise fails because required secrets and quotas are missing. Test the full recovery dependency chain and remediate gaps.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Copying one machine image proves full regional recovery. This is not a sound assumption; tested recovery of data identities dependencies and traffic handling.

lessons.takeaway: Recovery objectives must be measured in realistic exercises.
